 Judgment
Heard Sri.Hanumanthareddy Sahukar, learned counsel for the appellants - claimants and Smt.Anusha Sangami for Sri.S.K.Kayakamath for respondent - Insurance Company.
2. Though this appeal is listed for orders, with the consent of both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

3. Claimants in MVC No.567/2013 are before this Court challenging the validity of judgment and award passed in said case dated 30.06.2015 on the file of Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari insofar as inadequacy of compensation is concerned.
4.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ballari
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Admitted facts of the case are as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3409 One Honnurappa died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 23.04.2013 involving lorry bearing No.KA- 03/D-9915 when he was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing No.KA-35/R-5837.
Claimants being the wife and son of deceased, laid a claim before the Tribunal for awarding suitable compensation.

Rathanamma vs Shashavali S/O Asadulla Baig on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36929723/
2

5. Charge sheet came to be filed against the driver of lorry bearing No.KA-03/D-9915.
6.
Claim petition was resisted by filing necessary written statement by the respondents.
7. On contest, the claim petition came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.7,68,112/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
8. Being aggrieved by the inadequacy of quantum of compensation, claimants are in appeal.

9. Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, Sri.Hanumanthareddy Sahukar,
learned counsel for the appellants - claimants sought for NC: 2024:KHC-D:3409 enhancement of compensation following the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076 and Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another,
reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
10.

sentences.text: Per contra, Smt.Anusha Sangami on behalf of Sri.S.K.Kayakamath representing the Insurance Company supports impugned judgment by contending that as on the date of passing award, the Tribunal has taken into consideration relevant provisions of law which were prevailing at the relevant point of time and awarded just compensation and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

12. On such perusal of material on record, claimants have been successful in establishing that Honnurappa died on account of accidental injuries sustained in a road traffic accident occurred on 23.04.2013 involving motorcycle bearing No.KA-35/R-5837 and lorry bearing No.KA-03/D-9915.
13. Admittedly, there is no proper proof of income placed on record by the claimants to establish the monthly income of deceased Honnurappa.
14. Admittedly, in such circumstances, monthly income is to be assessed at Rs.7,000/-.
Deceased was aged 45 years.
Therefore, claimants are entitled for 25% addition towards future prospects.
Since he has got two dependants, 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Considering the age of the deceased, appropriate multiplier would be 14.

Claimants are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency as under:
Rathanamma vs Shashavali S/O Asadulla Baig on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36929723/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Rs.7,000 (income) + 25% (addition) - 1/3rd (deduction) x 12 (months) x 14 (multiplier) = Rs.9,80,112/-
16.
Claimants are entitled to Rs.30,000/- on conventional head and Rs.40,000/- each on filial affection.
In all, claimants are entitled to Rs.10,90,112/-.

17. In view of the foregoing discussion, following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed.
(ii) Impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal stands modified.
(iii) As against Rs.7,68,112/- awarded by the Tribunal, claimants are entitled to Rs.10,90,112/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:3409
( iv) It is made clear that claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 237 days.
(v) Insurance Company is granted four weeks time to deposit the compensation.
